title: Soil moisture increased the ozone injury response of bioindicator plants at the same eastern US forest biosites in 1994-2010, but ozone alone did not predict year-to-year injury
abstract: Question: does growing-season soil moisture change how much visible foliar injury a given ozone exposure causes in forest bioindicator plants? Approach: we used US Forest Service FIA ozone biomonitoring scores at 1,276 biosites (7,036 biosite-years, 1994-2010) in the Northeast, North Central and Pacific US. We calculated W126 exposure at each biosite from EPA AQS hourly ozone and used June-August NOAA CPC soil-moisture anomalies, with climate-division PDSI and Palmer Z as alternatives. Linear probability models with biosite fixed effects compared years at the same site, with visit day and summer Tmax controls. Result: ozone alone did not predict year-to-year injury (-0.004 per 10 ppm-h W126, SE 0.027). The ozone x moisture interaction was +0.029 per 10 ppm-h per +1 SD soil moisture (SE 0.011, p = 0.007; year-block bootstrap 95% interval 0.005 to 0.047; conditional logit p = 0.0002). 10 ppm-h more W126 gave +0.081 injury probability in wet summers and +0.023 in dry summers. High-ozone years were drier and hotter at the same site (r = -0.41 and +0.55), so the two effects partly cancel. The interaction held for all moisture and exposure metrics and for blackberry, black cherry, milkweed, big-leaf aster and ash. It was clear in the Northeast, weaker in the North Central states and absent in the Pacific states. Limitations: a next-year ozone placebo also had a positive main effect, so the ozone main effect is confounded by trends or crew changes; interaction placebos were near zero. Only 1 of 6 region-period tests had p < 0.05. Exposure is interpolated from monitors, moisture is not site-measured, and missed injury cannot be measured. citations.reason: Smith, Morin and McCaskill 2012 (USFS GTR NRS-103) reported descriptively that yearly injury did not follow SUM06 and that high-ozone wet conditions had most injury; we test this with within-site panel models.
